methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $47M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Pivotal, a Growth-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Marcus Leng, operates in a sector represented by seven private peers including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public comparables exist in this narrow category. The company has raised capital backed by Page (total disclosed as private).

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total capital raised of $47M as a valuation proxy, a typical 1.2x step-up multiplier applied to Growth-stage progression yields $56M. Peer-median analysis was not viable; while seven same-sector companies exist, none satisfied clustering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) in sufficient quantity to produce reliable multiples. A broader sectoral median would introduce material bias given the wide dispersion in business models and capital intensity across autonomous systems.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $48M to $64M, with a median point estimate of $56M. This reflects a single-method triangulation with constrained comparability data. Primary uncertainties include the representativeness of stage-progression multiples absent transaction evidence in the Drones & Autonomous space, and the absence of direct peer revenue or growth metrics to validate the raised-capital proxy. Additional diligence on unit economics and competitive positioning within the autonomous segment would strengthen conviction.
